newsitem.title: USA: USDA trade adviser to go to Brussels on meat issue.
newsitem.headline: USDA trade adviser to go to Brussels on meat issue.

text.p: The trade adviser to U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said he would leave later Wednesday for Brussels for meat-inspection negotiations.

Several hundred millions of dollars in U.S. meat exports to the European Union were at stake in the discussions over so-called veterinary equivalency rules. An interim pact was due to expire December 31.

Trade adviser Paul Drazek said there was "substantial" progress and he would be in Brussels, the EU headquarters, for two days. At the least, USDA officials would like additional time for discussions without a trade interruption.
The dispute was a top issue during a meeting earlier this week between President Clinton and top EU officials. According to one source, ag trade occupied 25 minutes of the meeting.
An "equivalency" agreement would allow each side to accept the other's products even if they disagree on particulars of how to assure safety.

In an interview Tuesday with Reuters, Glickman said he was encouraged by the tone of the White House meeting. But, he said the EU was "demanding rather unreasonable things from us right now" so an extension might be appropriate if long-term agreement was elusive.
